newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin not due back at work before month's end.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin not due back at work before month's end.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, suffering from pneumonia, will spend at least another three days in hospital and will need a three-week rehabilitation period after that, a top Kremlin doctor said on Friday.
Sergei Mironov, head of the Kremlin medical centre, also told a news briefing that the schedule of Yeltsin's planned foreign trips could be amended.
"It is difficult to plan but I think he will be another three days here," Mironov said. "To be honest, we have not yet reached a resolute breakthrough."
Asked whether Yeltsin would be able to travel abroad, Mironov answered: "I think yes, but dates could be changed."
Mironov said the three-week recovery period "does not mean isolation at a residence", but made clear he did not expect Yeltsin to return to the Kremlin before the end of the rehabilitation period.
Yeltsin was admitted to hospital on Wednesday night, only two weeks after returning to work following a major heart operation on November 5.
Mironov said Yeltsin had been advised to enter hospital earlier, but was reluctant to follow doctors' advice.
"He should have been brought here a few days earlier and we proposed this," Mironov said.
"But it is possible to understand him purely psychologically. The man had just recovered from one very serious problem when a second one appeared, though it was a smaller one.

"I understand him as a person but as a doctor I have another position. Of course I cannot say Boris Nikolayevich feels comfortable spiritually. Of course this is depressing him, of course his mood is not a very happy one but I see no reason for particular pessimism."
